subject: Clarifying: transient inference degradation impacting us-west (Summit Health)
content:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Brendan O'Rourke <brendan@sumhealth.com>
Cc: support@sumhealth.com
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying: transient inference degradation impacting us-west (Summit Health)

Hi Brendan / Summit Health team,

Quick note to let you know we’re observing a transient increase in p95 latency and a small number of 502 responses for hosted inference serving in the us-west region (us-west-2) that may be affecting some Summit Health production requests. We opened an internal incident and have put a short notice on our status page (link below).

What we see now:
- Window: ~08:10–08:45 PDT
- Symptom: p95 token latency elevated by ~2.1x; ~1.5% of requests returned 502
- Scope: subset of inference model variants (large-chat-2) routed to us-west pool

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Temporarily routing new Summit Health requests away from the affected pool to us-east while we triage
- Collecting traces and request IDs for any 502s (attached: live-traces-usw2-0821.zip)

As we triage I’ll loop in our infra/serving leads and keep you updated. Can you confirm whether you saw retry handling kick in on your side or if traffic dropped for any customer-facing endpoints? Any impact details you can share (sample request ids, timestamps) will speed root-cause.

Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-04-09-usw2-inference-variance

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

---
From: Brendan O'Rourke <brendan@sumhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying: transient inference degradation impacting us-west (Summit Health)

Hi Neha—thanks for the heads up.

We did start seeing elevated error rates around 08:12 and routed some traffic to a degraded read-only endpoint as a safety valve. User-facing degradation was limited to a small cohort of requests (we estimate ~12–18% of affected RPS for a 30-minute window). Our engineers captured a handful of failing request_ids and timestamps; I’ve pasted two sample IDs below:
- req_20270409_usw2_4421
- req_20270409_usw2_4478

We implemented short exponential-backoff retries on the client which reduced visible errors. Happy to share our traces if useful. Please let us know the remediation plan and ETA to return to normal.

-Brendan
Brendan O'Rourke
Senior Platform Engineer, Summit Health

---
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:37:40 -0700
Subject: RE: Clarifying: transient inference degradation impacting us-west (Summit Health)

Neha / team—quick triage update from infra/serving:

Observed behavior:
- The autoscaler for the us-west serving pool underpredicted short-term load after a small traffic spike; warm instances did not come up fast enough, leading to increased queuing and a small fraction of requests timing out and returning 502s.
- We also saw a concurrent kernel scheduling delay due to a recent runtime scheduler change that amplified tail latency for cold-started workers.

Actions in-flight (already executed):
- Reroute Summit Health traffic to us-east (minimizes further customer impact)
- Reverted the scheduler tweak that increased scheduling latency (rollout ID: rollout-20270408-rt1)
- Temporarily increased min replicas for us-west pool and enabled pre-warm policy for the next 60 minutes (should smooth ramp)

Next steps:
- Continue trace collection and correlate with Brendan’s sample IDs
- Run a controlled traffic replay in a canary to validate the revert
- If stable, we’ll reintroduce the change behind feature flag and monitor p95 for 1 hour before full rollback

Attaching a short log snippet and the trace bundle we collected.

Hannah Schmitt
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

---
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Brendan O'Rourke <brendan@sumhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 12:00:05 -0700
Subject: Status update & status page copy (us-west transient)

Hi Brendan—Neha, Hannah, Monica,

Wanted to give you the wording we’ve posted and pushed to our status page and to let you know where things stand:

Status page entry (posted 12:00 PDT):
"Incident 2027-04-09: transient elevated latency and partial error responses in us-west-2. We observed elevated p95 latency and a small percentage of 502 responses impacting a portion of hosted inference requests. Mitigation: routing impacted customer traffic to alternate regions and adjusting autoscaling policies. Engineers reverted a scheduler change that contributed to tail latency. Services are currently returning to expected performance. We will continue to monitor and will follow up with a postmortem."

Current status: Mitigation completed, routing stable to us-east, p95 latency trending back to normal (within baseline).
ETA for full recovery: ongoing monitoring for the next 2 hours; if stable we will mark resolved and begin a postmortem draft to share findings and long-term mitigations.

Public link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-04-09-usw2-inference-variance

Internal next steps: postmortem doc (owner: Hannah), schedule 90-minute RCA review with Summit Health if they’d like deeper detail (owner: Neha).

Sean Gallagher
Director, Product Reliability
Redwood Inference

---
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Brendan O'Rourke <brendan@sumhealth.com>, support@sumhealth.com
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 15:36:12 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: mitigation complete and postmortem next steps (Summit Health)

Brendan—thanks again for the quick signal and sample ids. We’ve confirmed mitigation actions and are not seeing further 502s for Summit Health traffic routed to us-east.

Next steps:
- We’ll share the draft postmortem (high level + timeline + permanent mitigations) by Monday 2027-04-12 EOD Pacific.
- If Summit Health would like a deep-dive technical review (RCA walkthrough with logs/traces), we can schedule a 90-minute session next week (please share preferred windows).

If you’d like us to redact any customer-specific fields in the postmortem before sharing internally at Summit Health, call that out and we’ll accommodate.

Appreciate the collaboration—we’ll keep monitoring and will follow up if anything new shows up.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
